docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Arr is a sixteen-knob polyphonic control-voltage source. Each knob sets one output channel. Arr can quantize those voltages to a scale or a fraction grid and shows knob values as voltages, note names, or fractions to match. Expanders can select ranges, combine Arr's channels with other voltages, and route or remove individual channels.

docs.title: Voltage knobs
docs.text:
Sixteen knobs set the sixteen channels of the polyphonic output. When a quantization mode is active, the output receives quantized voltages. The numbered voltage-range switch sets their magnitude, and ± switches between unipolar and bipolar ranges.

Knob value displays follow the active mode: raw voltages; note names using ♯ or ♭ for the selected scale and root; or fraction forms such as 3 * 1/4.

docs.title: Quantization modes
docs.text:
Click the top display to select the quantization mode:

Mode Behavior Off Knobs and the output pass voltages without quantization. Scale Quantizes to the selected musical scale and root note. Fraction Quantizes voltages to an absolute step of numerator / denominator volts. Ranged fraction Quantizes voltages to a step of numerator / denominator of the magnitude, in either polarity: 1/4 of 5 V is 1.25 V in 0–5 V and in ±5 V.

Click the two displays below it to set the mode's details: type and root in Scale, num and den in the fraction modes.

docs.title: Re<sup>x</sup> voltage-sequence transform
docs.text:
Rex gives Arr a movable window onto its polyphonic values.

start selects the first channel, and length sets how many channels it contains. The selection wraps around the channels of Arr’s polyphonic output.

docs.title: In<sup>x</sup> voltage operations
docs.text:
Inx lets you replace, add to, or insert Arr's output channels.

Each input on Inx corresponds to a channel of Arr’s polyphonic output. Its mode switch has three settings:

  • Overwrite: values from connected inputs replace the corresponding Arr voltages. Only the first channel of a polyphonic input is used.
  • Add: values from connected inputs are added to the corresponding channels of Arr’s output. Only the first channel of a polyphonic input is used.
  • Insert: all values from a connected polyphonic input on Inx are inserted before the corresponding Arr output channel. If insertion would produce more than 16 channels, Arr truncates the result to 16 channels.

Arr quantizes the result, so adding a CV transposes within the selected scale.

docs.title: Out<sup>x</sup> breakouts and Cut
docs.text:
Outx routes Arr's channels to separate destinations. It can route individual values and normalled ranges, or remove those values from the final polyphonic output.

Outx has two independent mode switches. nrm. selects how connected ports receive channels. cut selects whether those channels remain on Arr's output.

  • Individual: each connected port outputs the Arr value corresponding to its channel.
  • Normalled: each connected port outputs the range after the preceding connected port through its own channel, including unconnected channels in that range.
  • Copy: all channels remain on Arr's output.
  • Cut: channels sent to connected Outx ports are removed from Arr's output. With nrm. set to Individual, the remaining channels close up. With nrm. set to Normalled, only channels after the last connected port remain.

docs.title: Context menu
docs.text:
Snap to quantized values makes the knobs step between quantized values while you turn them.

Control rate trades control response for CPU; see Control rate.

docs.title: Two chords and a bass from a moving window over a quantized pitch table
docs.text:
Use Arr as a quantized pitch table. Connect an LFO to Rex's Start input so the window moves over the pitches. Then use Outx to break out a three-tone chord, a two-tone chord, and a bass to separate oscillators.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Bank is a sixteen-button polyphonic gate source. Each button sets one channel of the output.

docs.title: Gate buttons
docs.text:
out outputs the retained pattern in order, up to sixteen channels. Expanders can change the output without changing the button states.

The numbered switch sets the voltage magnitude; ± selects unipolar or bipolar output.

The lights show stored button states: an on button is bright when selected and dim otherwise; an off button is unlit.

docs.title: Re<sup>x</sup> gate-pattern transform
docs.text:
Rex gives Bank a movable window onto its gate pattern.

start selects the first gate; length sets the gate count. The selection wraps around the pattern.

docs.title: In<sup>x</sup> gate operations
docs.text:
Inx lets you replace, insert, or apply logical AND to Bank's gates.

Inx inputs are treated as gates: ≥1 V is high, ≤0.1 V is low. Between these thresholds, the previous state is retained.

Each input on Inx corresponds to a gate position of Bank's polyphonic output. Inx has three modes:

  • Overwrite: gate states from connected inputs replace the corresponding Bank gates.
  • Insert: all gate states from a connected polyphonic input are inserted before the corresponding Bank gate. If insertion would produce more than 16 positions, Bank truncates the result to 16 positions.
  • AND: a high input preserves the corresponding Bank gate, and a low input clears it.

Overwrite and AND use the first channel of each input. Unconnected inputs leave the corresponding Bank gates unchanged.

With Rex and Inx together, Bank applies them in physical left-to-right order.

docs.title: Out<sup>x</sup> breakouts and Cut
docs.text:
Outx routes Bank's gates to separate destinations. It can route individual gates and normalled ranges, or remove those gates from Bank's polyphonic output.

nrm. selects Individual or Normalled; cut selects Copy or Cut.

  • Individual: each connected port outputs the Bank gate corresponding to its position.
  • Normalled: each connected port outputs the positions after the preceding connected port through its own position, including unconnected positions. Positions beyond a shorter result carry Bank's low voltage: 0 V in unipolar mode, or the negative magnitude in bipolar mode.
  • Copy: all positions remain on Bank's output.
  • Cut: connected positions are removed from Bank's output. In Individual mode, the remaining positions close up. In Normalled mode, only positions after the last connected port remain. A port beyond the current result has no effect.

docs.title: Context menu
docs.text: Control rate trades control response for CPU; see Control rate.

docs.title: Trigger merger with manual mutes
docs.text: Place Inx on Bank's left, set mode to AND, and connect monophonic trigger signals to its inputs. Bank merges them into one polyphonic signal at out. Turn a Bank button on to pass the corresponding trigger signal, or off to mute it.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Coerce quantizes a polyphonic signal to the values of another polyphonic signal. It can operate in T&H mode or S&H mode.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
Values presented at in are quantized to the values presented at quant.. With trig connected, Coerce operates in S&H mode instead of T&H mode.

Choose the type of quantization from the context menu:

  • Octave Fold (default): each quant. value repeats in every octave, 1 V apart.
  • Restrict: only the exact quant. values are used.
  • Up: the nearest value at or above the input. With Restrict, an input above the highest value gets the highest.
  • Closest (default): the nearest value.
  • Down: the nearest value at or below the input. With Restrict, an input below the lowest value gets the lowest.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Mem is a polyphonic sample-and-hold memory whose addresses are arbitrary voltages, not numbered slots. It stores up to 64 addresses, each with up to 16 channels, and reads the closest.

docs.title: Inputs and output
docs.text:
Addresses are arbitrary voltages, not numbered slots. The write address addr. stores the polyphonic Data in at its current voltage. The read address addr. selects the closest stored address for output out. Exactly halfway between two stored addresses, the lower one is read. Reading empty memory gives 0 V. Each address input is monophonic.

The write trigger write and read trigger read accept either mono or polyphonic triggers. A mono write stores every channel present at in, and the address takes that channel count; a mono read restores all stored channels. Polyphonic write triggers update only their corresponding channels. Polyphonic read triggers update only their corresponding output channels.

With either trigger input unconnected, a change at its matching address input performs a full write or full read. The Data output holds its value until a read occurs.

docs.title: Behavioral notes
docs.text:
• A mono write replaces an existing equal address, or the nearest address when storage is full.
  • Polyphonic writes do not reduce a stored address's channel count.
  • Polyphonic reads do not reduce the output channel count; channels absent from stored data read as 0 V.
  • reset clears all stored addresses. A write trigger at the same moment is ignored. With write unconnected, nothing is written until the write address changes. With read unconnected, out drops to 0 V.
  • Mem saves its stored addresses and the current out voltages with the patch. Initialize keeps them; use reset to clear memory.

docs.title: Store and recall controller settings
docs.text:
Put Mem between a MIDI controller and the patch it controls. In VCV MIDI-CC, merge the knob outputs into in and split out to the patch. Patch one CC to both addr. inputs and set a row of buttons to send it on press, each with its own value. Patch a store button's CC to write. Turn off Smooth CC in MIDI-CC's menu so addresses don't glide.

Each address button recalls its settings at out; the store button saves the current knobs there. A crossfader between the merged knobs and out blends the live controller with the memory.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: With write unconnected, reopening a patch writes nothing while the write address stays the same. If the address source starts at another voltage when the patch loads and then returns to its saved voltage, Mem treats the return as an address change and overwrites that address with in. Connect write to keep stored values intact across reloads.
